name: Noru Signal Windbreaker
description:
A slim-cut windbreaker in black with thin horizontal stripes in electric blue — a subtle design that reads as athletic from a distance and slightly editorial up close. The shell is a lightweight ripstop nylon with a DWR finish. Chest pocket doubles as a stuff sack. Noru is a Tier 3 brand that sits between sport and street, popular in the mid-city neighborhoods where people actually run and also actually go out afterward. The fit is tailored enough to look intentional but relaxed enough to move in.

This jacket has an integrated thin-film solar weave on the shoulders and upper back — invisible in the fabric pattern — that trickle-charges whatever device is in the chest pocket. Not fast. Not impressive. But your phone will be at 40% instead of 12% when you get where you're going.
functionality: Integrated solar weave on shoulder and upper-back panels provides passive trickle charge to devices stored in chest pocket. Output is minimal — approximately 2W peak — sufficient for maintaining device charge during daily activity.
what_it_says: You're active, you're aware of your environment, and you invest in small conveniences that add up over a day.
story_hooks: Noru's solar weave is compatible with a specific aftermarket mod that converts it from trickle-charger to passive signal scanner — a conversion manual is circulating underground
Three Noru windbreakers were found at a safe house; the solar weave had been deliberately shorted in a pattern that looks like it might encode something
A Tier 3 runner who wore this jacket every morning vanished from her usual route — her jacket was found on a bench, charge indicator still blinking
